summary: Scott Alexander notes AI forecasters now match top humans and asks what cheap, instant expert forecasts could do for governments and institutions. A practical agenda for using them well.

title: The Data Is the Target
summary: As militaries lean on AI for decisions, the data feeding those systems becomes a prime target for adversaries. CSET researchers argue protecting that data is now a core defence task.

title: Biodata Matters for the Genesis Mission
summary: CSET argues the federal Genesis Mission, which uses AI to speed up science, needs a deliberate plan for biological data. Access to good biodata will decide how much AI helps medicine.

title: Getting it right
summary: Two essays on the 'invisible conspiracy' of people who sometimes act for the common good, and how institutions channel it. An optimistic take on moral progress.

title: At least it remembers
summary: Parents fear what AI will do to children, but for some children an AI companion is the only steady presence they have. Tom Wooldridge argues that absence of adults is the real problem AI exposes.

title: The Ground Beneath the Cloud: Dispersion and Dependency in the Digital Age
summary: Cloud dispersion has made digital services resilient to local outages, but it also concentrates dependence on a few providers and physical chokepoints. A security view of the infrastructure AI runs on.

title: Between Psyche and Cyborg: Carl Jung’s Legacy and the Countercultural Courage to Reclaim the Deeply Human in a Posthuman Age
summary: Traces Carl Jung's influence on the counterculture's attempt to reconcile spirit and machine. Background for current debates on technology and meaning.

title: Pacing AI via Compute Reallocation
summary: LessWrong repost of the AI Futures Project proposal to pace AI by reallocating compute. The discussion thread adds critiques and alternatives.

title: Pacing AI via Compute Reallocation
summary: The AI Futures Project proposes slowing the AI frontier by shifting compute from frontier training to other uses, rather than banning work outright. A concrete version of the pacing idea now circulating in policy circles.

title: The Silent Consensus
summary: In a Harvard lecture, Dean Ball argues against forfeiting a positive vision of the AI future and says the technology world already holds one. A big-picture case for where AI could take society.

title: What China’s Gene-Editing Deaths Reveal About Its Biotech Industry
summary: Reports on deaths in Chinese gene-editing trials and what they reveal about how the country's biotech industry is regulated. A cautionary tale on speed versus safety in new medicine.

title: The Moral Mandate for AI Non-consciousness
summary: Erik Hoel argues that building AI that cannot be conscious is a moral requirement, and answers objections to his proposal. Avoids creating minds that could suffer while capabilities keep rising.

title: What “Safe Robot” Means
summary: Imagines elder care in 2036 to ask what 'safe' should mean for household robots. As ageing societies turn to robots for care, safety standards become a welfare question.

title: Putting Pacing Into Practice
summary: Anton Leicht looks at the growing idea of pacing frontier AI and what it would take to make it workable in practice. Useful on why the consensus is fragile and who would have to agree.

title: Anthropic prices initial public offering
summary: Anthropic has priced its IPO of Class A common stock, a landmark capital-markets event for a frontier AI lab. It signals how much money and scrutiny now surround the platform vendors that AI products build on.

title: Who Pays for What We Know
summary: AI firms now produce most of what is known about AI, echoing Gilded Age industries that funded their own research. Palladium asks who should pay for independent knowledge about the technology.

title: The Part About the Machines
summary: An award-winning Peruvian novel was flagged as 99 percent AI-written, and its publisher stood by it. The essay asks what authorship and literary prizes mean once machines can write.

title: J.R.R. Tolkien on Fairy Tales, Language, the Psychology of Fantasy, and Why There’s No Such Thing as Writing “For Children”
summary: Tolkien on fairy tales, language and why fantasy is a serious human need. A Marginalian tour of his essay On Fairy-Stories.

title: AI agents are self-enacting storybooks of human culture
summary: Henry Farrell and Cosma Shalizi argue AI agents are best seen as cultural technologies that act out patterns from human stories. A frame that moves the debate away from minds and toward culture.

title: The horse made the state
summary: Argues the state was made possible by transport and the conquest it enabled, from the steppe to the sea, not by grain farming. A challenge to a standard story of how civilisation began.

title: No matter how you ask, more Americans are negative than positive about AI
summary: Our World in Data compares five large surveys and finds more Americans are negative than positive about AI, however the question is worded. Public sentiment is a real constraint on how fast AI spreads.

title: Recursive, Self, Improvement
summary: Traces the idea of an intelligence explosion from I.J. Good's 1965 paper to today's AI-assisted research. Separates what 'recursive self-improvement' meant then from what is happening now.

title: An update on our recent security incident
summary: Cursor shares findings from a two-week investigation of a recent attack and its impact. Useful case study on supply-chain risk for AI coding tools.

title: GPT-6 Cyber Versus Linux, The Problem With LLM-Powered Search, LLMs Edit Model Weights, Agentic Doc Retrieval
summary: An issue on agent harnesses, weaknesses of LLM-powered search, models editing their own weights and document retrieval for agents. Skim for the retrieval angle.

title: AI Company Employees Should Unionize
summary: Scott Alexander argues safety-minded staff at AI labs should organise rather than quit in protest. Because they are hard to replace, collective action could give them real say over how AI is built.

title: AI Kill Switches: What Policymakers Should Know
summary: CSET explains what it would actually take to shut off an AI system that is causing harm, and where kill-switch proposals fall short. A practical primer for a debate often held in slogans.

title: What Huawei’s Horinger data center reveals about China’s compute gap
summary: Epoch AI uses Huawei's new data centre to estimate how far China's AI compute trails the US under export controls. Cheap energy helps China, but chips remain the bottleneck.

title: Introducing: Qualiaphobic AI
summary: Erik Hoel proposes 'qualiaphobic' AI architectures designed to repel consciousness, like hostile architecture for minds. He presents it as a route to a good future where AI keeps improving.

title: Why anything exists
summary: Andrew Brenner offers a new answer to why there is something rather than nothing. Careful metaphysics on one of philosophy's oldest questions.

title: Shunning people who ‘look homeless’ is an aesthetic injustice
summary: Giacomo Floris argues that shunning people who look homeless is an aesthetic injustice. Access to haircuts, showers and clean clothes is owed as justice, not charity.

title: OK If Kids Grow Up Fast?
summary: Robin Hanson asks why people treat AI successors differently from biological descendants. A provocation on what we owe, and fear from, minds we create.

title: Piggybacking to the Frontier
summary: US data firms are selling about half a billion dollars of training data a year to Chinese AI labs. Training data, not just chips, is becoming a national-security question.

title: India is quietly doing great
summary: Noah Smith argues India's economy is quietly outperforming while attention is on China. A look at growth, manufacturing and how a large country climbs out of poverty.

title: Escaping The “Outside Criticism” Trap
summary: Scott Alexander dissects a rhetorical trap: accusing any group of ignoring 'outside' critics, however much it engages. On how to tell real closed-mindedness from an unfalsifiable charge.

title: Ethan Mollick on AI: Where Are We Now and Where Are We Headed
summary: Eric Topol interviews Ethan Mollick on where AI stands and where it is heading, including what it means for medicine and professional work. Two careful observers on the gap between capability and adoption.

title: The missing quadrant in responses to AI
summary: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor launch STABL, a lab studying the bottlenecks between AI capability and real societal change. They argue institutions, not models, will set the pace, and need reform backed by evidence.

title: When AIs Become Unruly Swarms
summary: Oxford and Cosmos Institute researchers argue that aligning AI models one at a time is not enough once agents collaborate. Safety will depend on the shared environment and rules those agents operate in.

title: Iron Makes Iron
summary: Dean Ball separates two kinds of recursive self-improvement after METR's study of AI speeding up research at Anthropic. He argues the fear of a runaway loop rests on the wrong kind.

title: Q3.5 Timelines Update: Looks Like the Intelligence Explosion Will Happen in 2027 After All
summary: The AI Futures Project updates its forecast and now expects an intelligence explosion in 2027. The authors explain which recent evidence moved their model.

title: Winning Time: Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces and the New Dimension of War
summary: How Ukraine chose to create a separate armed-forces branch for unmanned systems, and what that changed. A case study in militaries reorganising around drones and autonomy.

title: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI
summary: Ethan Mollick tests Claude Fable 5.2 and concludes it is almost AGI, or what he calls jagged AGI: expert at many tasks yet still behind humans in some. A grounded read on how close general AI is.

title: In Defense of Pulling Numbers Out of Thin Air
summary: Richard Chappell defends putting rough numbers on moral trade-offs, even subjective ones. Stated weights reveal how you would judge many cases, much as betting odds reveal beliefs.

title: New Units of Knowledge
summary: If everyone has an AI genie that does what they ask, Kevin Kelly asks what we still need from other people. An essay on what knowledge and exchange look like when answers are free.

title: The ethics of having a good time at Disney World, Florida
summary: Does the profit-driven corporation behind Disney World undermine the value of the joy people find there? A light piece of applied ethics.

title: How Low-Dimensional Is Intelligence?
summary: Robin Hanson asks whether intelligence is a few general skills or many specific ones. The answer decides whether a system superhuman in a few areas is superhuman everywhere.

title: Why the Cyberpocalypse Might Hit China Harder
summary: Chang Che argues that AI models finding software bugs at scale could hurt China more than the US. A different angle on who loses when vulnerability discovery gets cheap.

title: Gemini 4 Carbon Heads Toward Wider Availability, What Anthropic's IPO Means for Developers, Genie 4 Combines with Gemini to Train Robots
summary: Covers wider rollout of a Gemini model, what Anthropic going public means for developers, and a robot-training result. Gives a sense of where vendors are heading.

title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
summary: OpenAI and Cisco release an open-source runtime to shield Linux systems while patches roll out. Infra security news with indirect relevance.

title: Introducing SWE-2 Flash
summary: Cognition introduces SWE-2 Flash, a fast, low-cost coding model. Mainly a model-release note for coding agents.

title: Zombie Agents, Vampire Models, Witch Hunts, and the Mummy's Curse: AI Fears for Halloween 2026
summary: A Halloween issue that frames current AI worries as monsters, from runaway agents to policy backlash. Light reading with little operational value.

title: Corridor is Joining Cognition
summary: Security startup Corridor is joining Cognition to build out Devin Security. A small acqui-hire move.

title: Scattered thoughts on how doing math feels these days
summary: A mathematician records what doing research feels like as AI starts proving theorems. A time capsule of expert work changing in real time.

title: FrontierCode 2.0
summary: Cognition launches FrontierCode 2.0, a benchmark with more diverse, harder tasks across more repositories. Helpful for judging coding-agent claims.

title: Some Memories of Early Anthropic
summary: A former employee recalls Anthropic between late 2022 and mid 2023, rendered from memory. A rare inside view of the company's culture before it became a frontier giant.

title: Anthropic files S-1 with the SEC for proposed initial public offering
summary: Anthropic's filing with the SEC for its public offering, the first formal disclosure of its financials and risks. The details inform how much room AI vendors have to compete on price.

title: Meta’s Muse Wonder and Spark Open, Educational Use of ChatGPT, Reflection's Partnership with Nvidia
summary: Issue covering Meta's open Muse releases, classroom use of ChatGPT and a lab's partnership with Nvidia. A general roundup with limited relevance.

title: Introducing the Agent SDK
summary: Cursor releases the Agent SDK it uses internally for managed agents like Bugbot, letting you define agents in code and deploy with one command. Signals how agent platforms are being productized.

title: Investing in the public benefit
summary: Anthropic is putting part of its shares into a new public benefit fund whose stake grows with the company. An early test of whether AI wealth can be tied to public good.

title: Cursor is now a part of SpaceX
summary: Cursor announces it has been acquired by SpaceX. A major consolidation of the AI coding-tool market that reshapes the competitive landscape for AI developer tooling.

title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1
summary: Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 upgrades its multimodal reasoning model with better tool use for agent tasks. Another frontier lab pushing agent-oriented models, which shapes what tool-calling clients will hit a data API.

title: Introducing Muse Image and Muse Video
summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs releases an image model and previews a video model, both tied to social context. Mostly consumer media generation.

title: From Brain Waves to Words: Brain2Qwerty Offers a New Path to Communication Without Surgery
summary: Meta shares a second-generation system that decodes typed text from brain signals without implants. Interesting research, but far from the data platform world.

title: Introducing Muse Spark: Scaling Towards Personal Superintelligence
summary: The launch post for Meta Superintelligence Labs' first Muse model, a natively multimodal reasoning model. Useful as the baseline for how Meta now competes at the frontier.

title: Reinforcement Learning Heats Up, White House Orders Muscular AI Policy, and more...
summary: An older issue about the reaction to DeepSeek, the rise of reinforcement learning and a White House AI policy order. Dated context rather than current news.
